component.name: RailReader2
component.summary: AI-guided rail reading PDF viewer for comfortable high-magnification reading

description.p: RailReader2 is a desktop PDF viewer with AI-guided "rail reading" mode for high-magnification viewing. It uses an ONNX layout-detection model to identify text blocks, then locks the viewport to one block at a time so the reader can comfortably read at very high zoom levels without losing context.
Features:

ul.li: AI-detected layout for rail-style line-by-line reading at high magnification
Optional OCR so scanned pages can be rail-read too
Annotations: highlight, underline, freehand, rectangle, text notes with spell checking
Portals that keep a cited figure or table in view while you read, and freeze panes for table headers
Split panes, tear-off windows and continuous scrolling
Named bookmarks, outline navigation, full-text search
Markdown export via VLM transcription of figures, tables, equations
Colour effects (high contrast, amber, invert) for vision comfort

screenshot.caption: Rail mode locks the view to one text block and advances line by line at high magnification
Line focus blur dims everything except the line being read
Highlight, underline, draw and add notes, stored in the PDF
Colour effects for visual comfort: high contrast, amber and invert
Multiple documents in tabs with an outline side panel

description.p: Annotations on PDFs that can't be written to, such as read-only or signed files, now stay with the document when you move, rename or copy it, just as portals and view rotation already do. Annotations saved before this update still load. The command-line tool finds them the same way. Exporting a PDF with annotations is also more reliable: you can keep annotating while the export runs.

Fixes from a code audit. Typing in a search or rename box no longer triggers rail keys or pastes annotations, and shortcuts like Escape, F11 and Ctrl+W still work while a text box has focus. After dragging a toolbar slider or toggling jump mode or auto-scroll, the arrow keys go straight back to the document. Resetting all settings and deleting a bookmark now ask first, deleting a portal can be undone, and Go to page keeps its box open with a message on a bad page number. PP-DocLayoutV3 GPU acceleration no longer silently falls back to the CPU, closing a tab during an export or while pages are still drawing no longer risks a crash, and figure and reference auto-pins update when OCR re-reads a page. The Index pane fills in its thumbnails faster.

Comments can now be answered. Reply to any annotation from its right-click menu, the Edit menu or the Comments pane, which shows each comment with its replies underneath. Replies are saved into the PDF as threaded comments, so other PDF readers show them nested too. Set your name under Settings, Reading, Annotations and it is saved with everything you write. Deleting a comment deletes its replies with it, and Undo brings them all back.

The reading guide is now an experimental feature and is hidden by default. To use it, turn on "Enable experimental features" under Settings, Reading (advanced view); the toolbar button, the Rail menu entry and the K key then appear. Your guide settings are kept either way.

Link peek: choose "Shows a preview" under Settings, Reading, Links, and clicking a link opens a small preview of where it goes (the reference, equation or figure it points at, in your colour effect) with a button to go there. Ctrl+click still follows the link directly, and Escape or a click elsewhere closes the preview.

A new setting (Settings, Reading, Links) chooses what clicking a link does: follow it, follow it only with Ctrl+click, or nothing, so a stray click while reading no longer jumps away. When a plain click won't follow a link, pointing at it says where it goes and how to follow it. Messages now briefly use the whole status bar, and tooltips everywhere sit beside their control instead of under the pointer, so they can no longer swallow a click.

Back and Forward buttons are now always in the status bar (and in the Navigation menu, on Alt+Left/Right and on the mouse side buttons), and Back returns to exactly where you were, including the zoom and the rail line. Following a link shows where it went with a one-click way back. Page changes at rail zoom no longer pause the app while the new page renders, double-clicking into rail mode lands on the line and spot you clicked, and status-bar buttons no longer ignore a click made while their tooltip is showing.

You can now change the colour of an existing annotation: right-click it and choose Colour, or use Edit, Annotation Colour. The line focus and line highlight toggles are remembered between sessions, and Ctrl+Shift+M now zooms back out to the margin-fit level even when you have zoomed in past it. Comments and notes started from the pop-out portal window no longer open behind it.

Scrolling pace now stays the same on screen at any magnification. Holding the arrow keys, auto-scroll and steering with Shift used to move faster the further you zoomed in and crawl when zoomed out; the speeds are now scaled to feel the same as at 7x.

Steering is calmer and easier to follow: a small indicator shows where the stick was planted and how far you are pushing (in the colours of the active colour effect), steering parks when it moves to a new line so you can find your place and re-centre the mouse, and a new Steer sensitivity setting tunes the throw. Double-clicking a highlight at rail zoom now opens its comment instead of zooming, dialogs no longer hide behind a fullscreen window, and Cancel is no longer clipped at larger font sizes.

The reading guide now steers rail mode too: hold Shift and nudge to scroll along the line with the word being read outlined and kept centred, step lines with a nudge up or down, and pause at equations, tables and new pages until you push again.

Reading Guide: a new pointer mode for reading at low magnification. Hold Shift and nudge the mouse to steer a word-by-word highlight along the text at your reading pace, like an invisible joystick; release to park it. Point-at-the-text and no-key variants are in Settings.

Merging highlights now checks up front whether a PDF is signed or read-only, so a reviewer's highlight is never merged away where the PDF can't be changed, and the check no longer pauses on large scanned files.
Comments on highlights: double-click a highlight to attach a note to it. Overlapping highlights of the same colour can be merged into one, by hand or automatically as you draw.
Copy, cut and paste notes, text boxes, rectangles and pen strokes within and between documents. Highlights stay on their text, and highlights from other PDF tools no longer hide the words underneath.
A simpler Settings window: the most-used settings by default, with everything else behind "Show advanced settings".
New welcome screen and a richer catalogue listing with screenshots.
Packaging changes for the AppImage catalogue.
Spell checking in text-note and free-text annotations.
Updated Avalonia to 12.1.3.
Smoother auto-scroll, tiled GPU texture upload and a Display GPU setting for hybrid-GPU laptops.
